text: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog, but that sentence alone is far too short for any reliable result, so this warmup request deliberately contains a longer passage of ordinary prose. Loading an ensemble of transformer models into GPU memory takes a little time, because each detector pulls its own tokenizer, configuration and weights into the cache before serving the very first score. By sending one detection request now, every backend is forced to initialize eagerly, so subsequent calls return quickly instead of paying that startup cost again. The text itself does not matter much for this purpose, yet it is written to be roughly two hundred words long, in plain standard English, without unusual punctuation or formatting, so that every model can chunk it cleanly and produce a stable, unsurprising answer. When this warmup finishes, the service is ready for real documents through the web interface, the JSON API and the command line tool alike.
